h1: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple: Fifth Joyful Mystery
intro: A little read-aloud book for one decade of the Rosary: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple.
shortAnswer: This book walks children through the Fifth Joyful Mystery, the Finding of Jesus in the Temple: a short story, the Gospel passage, the Our Father, ten Hail Marys and the Glory Be, and a reflection on perseverance in seeking Christ.
aboutHtml:
Painting: Albrecht Dürer, Jesus among the Doctors. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons. Image source (Wikimedia Commons).

The Gospel passage is quoted word for word from the Douay-Rheims Bible, 1899 American Edition, which is in the public domain; verse numbers are omitted for reading aloud, and … marks skipped verses. The Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be and Fatima prayers follow the standard formulas used across this site. This mystery is traditionally prayed on Monday / Saturday.

faq.q: What is the Fifth Joyful Mystery?
faq.a: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple. When Jesus was twelve, he stayed behind in the Temple, listening and asking questions, and Mary and Joseph searched for him for three days. This mystery is traditionally prayed on Monday / Saturday, and its fruit is perseverance in seeking Christ.

faq.q: How do you pray this decade with children?
faq.a: Read one page at a time. On the decade page, pray the Our Father once, the Hail Mary ten times (one for each bead), then the Glory Be and the Fatima prayer.
